## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet, and scores stay hidden for the whole search, so each candidate has to be a strong bet on its own. The budget rule rewards fewer PPO epochs: 2 epochs gives about 1.86x the samples of the default 4. With the default 4,096-sample updates, the default recipe gets only about 32 updates. The core skill is perceiving, for each brick and anchor, which layer the brick lands on and whether the cells it fills at that layer are target cells. The baseline mixes all layers in its 1x1 stem, which makes it hard to tell which layer a brick lands on. Round 1 tests three directions: (A) a recipe that gives more, smaller updates, with the baseline network unchanged; (B) a per-layer brick-scoring head that pools over each footprint, plus the cheaper recipe; (C) a deeper residual trunk with dilation and global context, which sees more of the grid.

### Round 2
Scores are hidden. All three round-1 trials trained without errors, but nothing ranks them. So I am spreading this round over three ideas the earlier trials did not test. (1) Reward timing: the +1 for an exact build arrives only when the episode ends. With gamma 0.95 that bonus is worth about 0.5 at the first placement of a 15-brick build, so a longer horizon may value it better. (2) A data-heavy recipe: one PPO epoch with large batches gives about 3x the starting sample count on fresh designs. (3) A cheap per-cell attention over layers. At each cell it can learn what sits at the build's current height, which decides where a brick lands and what it fills. This is cheaper than r1c2's per-layer footprint head, so it keeps more samples. Candidates 1 and 3 reuse r1c1's recipe, so each tests one change against it.

### Round 3
Scores are hidden, so the evidence so far is only that all six files trained within time and passed the checks. That includes the per-layer heads at r of about 1.8 and the 1-epoch recipe at 401k steps. I have no ranking to refine, so I'm choosing on priors and making sure the final set covers different plausible winners. I'm giving this the most weight: the agent must work out where a brick lands (the highest filled layer under its footprint) and whether the cells at that layer match the target. Per-layer heads model this directly. Recipe ideas worth keeping: more fresh samples (fewer epochs) and a longer horizon, because the +1 bonus comes only at the end. This round combines plausible changes that were each tested alone. It also adds one structured head: a learned 'landing layer' softmax over layers that weights a per-layer fill-quality score. P1 and P3 differ only in that head, so the comparison stays clean.

### Round 4
No scores are visible, so I can only reason about the design. Every trial trained without errors, so the time limit and compute cap are not binding at these sizes. Over three rounds the search explored two kinds of change. On the recipe side it tried fewer PPO epochs with more fresh samples, and a longer horizon (gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95) to carry the exact-build bonus back to early placements. On the architecture side it tried per-layer heads (logsumexp, then a landing-gated version), layer attention, and a deeper dilated trunk with global context. The strongest recipe idea, 1 epoch with 512 envs at long horizon, has only been tested on the starting network. The structural heads have only used 2 epochs with about 135k samples. Since this is the last round and the final pick goes to the best 2-seed score, the best bets pair the most promising structures with the data-heavy recipe, plus one low-risk recipe refinement on the starting network.
